rationale: Jude 1:6's 'angels who did not stay within their own domain but abandoned their proper dwelling... kept in eternal chains under darkness, bound for judgment' is read by a scholarly consensus dating to the mid-twentieth century, represented by Richard Bauckham's Word Biblical Commentary on Jude, as directly dependent on 1 Enoch 6-19's Watcher story -- an extrabiblical Second Temple elaboration of Genesis 6:1-4's 'sons of God' who 'saw that the daughters of men were beautiful' (6:2, BSB). Jude's own text names neither Genesis nor the phrase 'sons of God'; the link runs through 1 Enoch's development of that episode, not a direct citation of Genesis. Graded allusion, not explicit reference, because Jude does not cite Genesis itself; graded strong because the dependence on 1 Enoch's reworking of Genesis 6 is a well-evidenced scholarly reading of Jude's source material, not a speculative guess.
